description:
The substrate modules already live at Filament.* (Reconciler, Hooks, Fiber, FiberTree, RenderContext, VNode, Cell, Core, etc.). Web-specific surface lives at Filament.Web (to_iodata, to_rendered) and Filament.LiveView/LiveComponent/HTMLEngine. The split exists; it's just not enforced or documented.

Rather than churn through a rename for cosmetic effect (the parent epic's 'naming TBD' is settled by the existing names), this ticket:

1. Adds a documentation section that explicitly lists which modules are substrate (target-agnostic) vs web-specific.
2. Adds a compile-time sanity test that asserts substrate modules don't reference `Phoenix.LiveView.*` types or call `Phoenix.HTML.*` — fails CI if a future change accidentally pulls a Phoenix dep into Core.
3. Updates the relevant guides (events, cells, getting-started) with a 'modules' section pointing at the boundary.

No module moves. The proof of the split is the OctoPi consumer's ability to import only the substrate modules.

## Acceptance
- New test asserts substrate-module BEAMs don't reference Phoenix.LiveView modules.
- Documentation lists substrate vs web modules.
- mix test green; mix credo --strict clean; mix dialyzer 0 errors.
title: Phase 4: Document Core/Web boundary; lock the substrate against Phoenix imports
